_comment: Gates that declare an intent they are not wired for (vibe-ic#306/#316). MAY ONLY SHRINK. Fixing one changes what a real run blocks on — a flow-owner decision — so they are recorded, not silently enforced here.
undeclared_comment: Gates that are AUDIT_ONLY and declare NO intent at all (vibe-ic#886) — enforcement was never decided, which is a DIFFERENT defect from declaring one thing and being wired another, so it is a SEPARATE shrink-only register. Paid down by the gate stating `ENFORCEMENT:` / `verdict_mode`, or by a runner invoking it inline. NOT by deleting the entry: the audit recomputes this set on every run, so a deleted line comes straight back as NEW and fails.
undeclared_scope_expanded: vibe-ic#886: a SECOND register, undeclared_known, records gates that are AUDIT_ONLY and declare no intent at all. That class existed on every prior version of this audit and was structurally unable to fail it, so it is a wider scope over pre-existing debt, not new debt. vibe-ic#884 (2026-08-09) widened it again by 3, for the same reason and not because anything regressed: bsdl_emit, rtl_hygiene_lint and sdc_syntax_check were scored ENFORCED only because their FILENAME appeared in a runner string. Once ENFORCED required the exit status to reach a control-flow decision, all three were correctly reclassified AUDIT_ONLY, and — declaring nothing — they joined this register. Their status was always discarded; the audit simply could not see it. Paid down the same way as the rest: state an intent, or invoke the gate inline. NOT by deleting the entry. sdc_syntax_check HAS NOW BEEN PAID DOWN that way and its entry is removed: the runner's step-8 block, which bound the subprocess result and never read it, now reaches a decision on the exit status, so the audit scores the gate ENFORCED / INLINE_BLOCKING and no longer computes it into this register. The removal is the SHRINK the audit asked for, not a deletion of unpaid debt - a deleted line that was still owed comes straight back as NEW on the next run and fails. bsdl_emit and rtl_hygiene_lint are still owed and stay. sdc_syntax_check additionally carries a real hole worth its own issue: flow:1094-1098 declares both required_outputs reports/phase2/sdc_check.json and program_exit_zero, but the program writes that JSON UNCONDITIONALLY before exiting 1, so a project with no valid SDC still satisfies the presence gate and phase 2 proceeds.
